blocks.text: What are Peptides and How Do They Boost Energy?

Researchers believe the human body can live for 100–110 years. However, in most cases, modern humans live for 70–80 years. Of course, this is significantly longer than 100 years ago, when the average life expectancy was 40–45 years. If there is an opportunity to prolong life, why not take advantage of it? At the same time, it is necessary to adhere to an important principle: not simply to increase the age of old age, but to maintain active longevity, unburdened by serious illnesses. The solution to the problem lies in peptide bioregulation technologies, which help restore gene activity and the synthesis of the body’s own proteins in various pathologies and during aging.

Peptide bioregulators are not a new invention. Bioregulatory (short) peptides are natural substances consisting of 2–4 amino acid residues. In other words, they are not proteins, which contain more than 50 amino acids. Thanks to their small molecular weight and simple structure, short peptides can penetrate cells and the nuclear envelope without the need for receptor-mediated endocytosis. Bioregulatory peptides exert a complementary, gene-specific effect. This means that each of them is strictly specific to its own gene. Therefore, protein synthesis is regulated in a targeted manner, acting on cells of a particular type. Accordingly, peptides of the heart, brain, or cartilage, while helping to systematically renew the body, cannot affect other organs or tissues. Before starting peptide regulators, consult a doctor. For example, frequent colds do not always indicate breathing problems — they may be related to immune disorders. People over 45, as well as those who are constantly exposed to stress, overload, lack of sleep, or already have chronic diseases, have a particular need for peptides. Preventive intake of peptide complexes can prevent the onset of more serious ailments in adulthood. In addition, peptide complexes can solve many endocrine problems in a safe, non-hormonal way, which is also relevant for female biohackers.

blocks.text: MOTS-C

MOTS-C is a mitochondrial-derived peptide (MDP) consisting of 16 amino acids that plays a key role in regulating cellular metabolism. Synthesized within mitochondria, MOTS-C functions by modulating cellular energy balance through pathways related to glucose metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and cellular stress response. MOTS-C exerts its effects by moving to the cell nucleus, where it influences the expression of genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic regulation, especially under conditions of metabolic stress. [Studies have shown](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpendo.00249.2020) that this peptide improves physical endurance, reduces obesity and insulin resistance, and helps alleviate metabolic disorders and age-related diseases, including osteoporosis. MOTS-C promotes metabolic homeostasis and longevity, improves physical endurance, reduces obesity, insulin resistance, and other pathological processes such as osteoporosis.
SS-31 (Elamipretide)

SS-31, also known as elamipretide, is a synthetic peptide that targets the inner mitochondrial membrane to improve mitochondrial function by binding to the phospholipid cardiolipin. It works by stabilizing mitochondria, reducing oxidative stress, and enhancing ATP production, with potential therapeutic applications in various diseases linked to mitochondrial dysfunction, including heart failure, Barth syndrome, and some neurodegenerative conditions. Clinical trials are ongoing for some of these indications, and the most common side effect is a mild injection-site reaction.
Humanin

The natural endogenous micropeptide humanin and its derivatives protect cells from damage in neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease. The peptide is also active in ischemic heart disease, atherosclerotic plaques, eye diseases, and in improving bone tissue growth. Data on the relationship between humanin and oncogenesis and cancer metastasis appear contradictory. Clearly, further preclinical studies of the effects of the peptide in cancer are needed.
Epitalon

Epitalon exhibits a wide range of biological activity: it induces telomere elongation, slows the aging process, reduces the manifestations of atherosclerosis, and improves cognitive function regardless of age. This peptide also has anticancer activity in animal models.

Like epithalamine, epithalon increases melatonin production by the pineal gland (pineal body), as demonstrated in experiments on elderly monkeys and humans. During the tests, epitalon affected nighttime melatonin production, and its effectiveness was 500 times higher than that of epithalamine. The peptide normalized the daily rhythms of hypothalamic norepinephrine and dopamine production.

Biohacking peptides aimed at increasing endurance and physical performance are actively studied in sports medicine and [biohacking](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/what-is-biohacking). They help improve mitochondrial function, accelerate recovery, increase oxygen utilization, and reduce inflammation after exercise.

Tesamorelin
Tesamorelin is a synthetic peptide that stimulates the production of human growth hormone (HGH). This natural hormone supports overall well-being.

Tesamorelin has demonstrated the potential to reduce visceral adipose tissue (VAT), improve body composition, and enhance cognitive function by stimulating growth hormone secretion. There are also studies showing that the peptide helps maintain standard eye structure while enhancing the retina’s bioelectrical function, which is necessary for vision.

TB-500 (Thymosin Beta-4)

TB-500 is a peptide used to accelerate recovery from injuries and surgeries. It stimulates the activity of cells involved in tissue regeneration, particularly those in tendons, muscles, bones, and skin. TB-500 has anti-inflammatory properties, improves mobility, and supports joint function. It has a positive effect on arthritis and other inflammatory joint diseases.

The combination of BPC-157 and TB-500 also creates synergy, enhancing the restorative and regenerative properties of both peptides. This mixture is the subject of research aimed at studying its potential impact on recovery processes after physical exertion or other conditions.
Recovery & Tissue Repair Peptides
Recovery and tissue repair peptides are short chains of amino acids that accelerate healing by stimulating cell regeneration, reducing inflammation, and promoting blood vessel formation.
GHK-Cu (Copper Peptide)

GHK-Cu is a bioactive peptide, a tripeptide complex containing glycine-histidine-lysine bound to copper (Cu), hence its alternative name, “copper peptide,” due to the presence of copper in its composition.

A clinical study published in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology reports results from the use of GHK-Cu. They demonstrate their positive effects on skin texture, the reduction of signs of aging, and improvements in overall skin appearance.

GHK-Cu has a proven beneficial effect on the skin, stimulating the production of collagen and elastin, which make the skin healthier and more elastic. This peptide also improves cell regeneration and stimulates blood microcirculation in the skin, promoting faster healing of various injuries. GHK-Cu consists of glycine, L-histidine, and copper, which have a beneficial effect on improving skin elasticity and health.
Hydrolyzed Collagen Peptides
Collagen peptides are tiny pieces of protein from animal collagen. Collagen is one of the materials that make up cartilage, bone, and skin.

These peptides are produced by breaking down whole collagen molecules into smaller fragments. When taken by mouth, collagen peptides seem to build up in the skin and cartilage. This might help improve some skin and joint conditions.

Collagen peptides are used for dry skin, aging skin, and osteoarthritis. They are also used for osteoporosis, brittle nails, muscle strength, and many other purposes. Still, there is no good scientific evidence to support most of these uses.
Glutathione

Glutathione is a vital endogenous antioxidant involved in the direct neutralization of free radicals, the regeneration of other antioxidants, and phase II liver detoxification. [Studies](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4684116/) show that increased glutathione levels are associated with improved immune response, recovery from cellular stress, and overall cell resilience.
A stable redox balance, maintained by glutathione, is crucial for the functioning of all cellular components, including DNA integrity.

Summary

Peptides can be taken orally thanks to modern technologies that protect them from destruction in the stomach. Still, a doctor’s consultation is necessary to determine the dosage and duration of the course, especially in the presence of chronic diseases. Peptides can safely restore protein synthesis in cells, helping prevent early age-related changes. Taking peptides is usually recommended for prevention and maintenance of health, especially for people over 30 or those prone to stress and unfavorable environmental conditions, but specific indications and treatment regimens are determined by a doctor.
